newsitem.title: USA: Nova to buy Crestar business.
newsitem.headline: Nova to buy Crestar business.

text.p: Crestar Bank, a unit of Crestar Financial Corp, has signed a letter of intent to sell its merchant card processing business to Nova Information Systems Inc, the companies said Tuesday.

The deal is expected to be completed in the second quarter and is expected to add about $1.8 billion in annualized credit and debt card transaction processing volume to Nova's business, the companies said.
As a result of the transaction, Crestar said it expects to record an after-tax gain of $12 million in the second quarter.
The transaction will not affect Crestar first quarter results, which are scheduled for release April 10, it said.
Crestar Bank is based here and has branches in Virginia, Maryland and the District of Columbia.
Nova is an Atlanta, Ga.-based provider of merchant processing services.
Nova said the deal will add 11,000 additional locations to its customer base and 500 Crestar branches to its distribution network.
Nova Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Edward Grzedzinski said the transaction will make Nova the seventh largest merchant transaction processor in the U.S. It currently ranks No. 8.
